tasks.short: Check which job is next, gather tools, fixtures and material, preset tools and measure offsets, record offsets for the machine and prepare fixtures while the machine runs.

steps.what: CNC operator checks which future jobs come next on the schedule board
CNC operator gathers tools, fixtures and material for the next job
CNC operator presets tools and measures offsets while machines are operating
CNC operator records tool offsets for the machine: on a card today; after the change the presetter sends them to the control and the operator checks them there against the tool numbers
CNC operator prepares fixtures on the setup table

tasks.design: The machine terminal ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the next job from the schedule with a pick list of tools, fixtures and material and where they are stored. The tool presetter sends measured offsets straight to the machine control, so no offset cards are written. Gathering, presetting and preparing fixtures stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: The next job was read from a board, tools searched for and offsets written on cards.
tasks.enabler_now: Presetters send offsets to controls, and terminals show pick lists per job.
tasks.still_hard: Tools are not always where the list says.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing to set up the long job now because the short one may be cancelled.

reach.learn: Whether pick lists cut search time.

evidence.claim: Tool presetters can send measured offsets to CNC controls over the network.
Per-operator logs in shop-floor systems need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the schedule to ready fixtures; changeover is outside.
Input contract: schedule from the planner; tool locations kept by the tool crib; fallback is the board and cards.

Gathering, presetting and preparing fixtures stay manual. s3 keeps its full time because measuring is hands-on. s2 keeps 80 because the pick list shows where each item is stored, so less searching; s1 keeps 40 because the next job shows at the machine instead of on the board; s4 keeps 20 for checking the sent offsets against the tool numbers.
The presetter and controls are networked.

incremental.description: CNC operator updates tool locations when moving tools.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tool locations are not kept up to date, so the pick list does not cut searching and s2 keeps its full time (13.0); high: locations are kept and s2 keeps 80 (21.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Stop and look at the problem, call the supervisor or programmer, work out the fix together, get approval to continue and log the problem and fix.

steps.what: CNC operator stops the machine and looks at the problem
CNC operator takes a photo of the problem with the machine terminal
CNC operator checks the call before sending: the photo shows the problem, the alarm and job are the right ones and the right person is chosen
CNC operator sends the checked call with alarm, job and photo to the supervisor's or programmer's phone
CNC operator gets the supervisor or programmer to the machine: walks the floor to find them today; after the change waits at the machine for them to answer the call
CNC operator confers with supervisors or programmers to resolve machine malfunctions or production errors
CNC operator writes the problem and fix in the shift log: in a paper book today; after the change in a form on the terminal where the alarm, job and time fill from the call

tasks.design: The operator takes a photo at the machine terminal ({OPS_SYSTEM}), checks the call and sends the alarm, the job and the photo to the supervisor's or programmer's phone, so the operator does not walk the floor to find them. The supervisor records approval to continue on the terminal, and the log form on the terminal fills the alarm, job and time from the call while the operator still writes the problem and the fix. Looking at the problem and conferring stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Help was found by walking around, and problems were logged in a paper book.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop-floor terminals send calls with alarm data to phones.
tasks.still_hard: On night shifts nobody may be available to come.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a crash so the programmer sees what went wrong.

reach.learn: Whether logged fixes reduce repeat errors.

evidence.claim: Shop-floor terminals can send help calls with alarm data to phones.
Systems that can monitor staff presence or behaviour need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the alarm to the problem log; repair work is outside.
Input contract: alarms from the machine control; fix categories set by the production supervisor; fallback is walking and the paper book.

Looking, conferring and approving keep their full time, and so do the photo, the check and the send. s2 keeps 35 for waiting at the machine until help arrives; s5 keeps 75 because only the alarm, job and time fill from the call and the operator writes the problem and the fix.
Supervisors' time is outside the operator's savings.
research_questions: Does machine downtime per problem fall?

incremental.description: CNC operator follows up calls that nobody answers, mostly on night shifts, by phoning or walking.

approvals.approved_version: The call with the alarm, the job and the photo exactly as checked by the operator in s2c, sent once from the terminal to the chosen supervisor's or programmer's phone; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: supervisors miss many calls on the phone, so the operator still walks for about half of them and s2 keeps 70 (10.3); high: calls are answered and s2 keeps 35 (18.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the program disk or card, load it into the controller, call up the program, check the tool list against loaded tools and return the media.

steps.what: CNC operator finds the right disk or card in the program cabinet; after the change only for the older controls that read media only
CNC operator loads control media into the machine controller; after the change only on the older media-only controls
CNC operator enters commands into machine controllers to retrieve programmed instructions
CNC operator checks the program's tool list against the tools in the machine
CNC operator returns the disks and cards to the cabinet; after the change only for the older media-only controls

tasks.design: Programs are served to the control over the network from the program server ({OTHER}), so disks and cards are fetched, loaded and returned only for the older controls that read media only. Selecting the work order on the control calls up the program, and the control lists missing or mismatched tools against its tool table for the operator to check. The operator keeps the final check before running.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programs lived on disks and cards in a cabinet.
tasks.enabler_now: CNC controls load programs over the network and compare tool lists with the tool table.
tasks.still_hard: Old controls that only read media need a converter or stay as they are.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a worn tool is in the right pocket but should not be used.

reach.learn: Whether converting media-only machines pays back.

evidence.claim: CNC controls can load programs over a network and compare tool lists with the tool table.
Learning models in machine safety functions need third-party assessment; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work order to stored media; running the job is outside.
Input contract: programs released by the CNC programmer on the server; fallback is disks and cards.
The operator still checks tools before running.
About 80% of the controls take programs over the network; the older media-only controls keep disks and cards, so finding, loading and returning media keep 20.

already_counted.description: CNC operator reviews the tool mismatch list.

incremental.description: CNC operator logs in at the control.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the controls are networked, so s1, s2 and s5 keep 50 (49.0); high: 80% of controls are networked as assumed (67.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The CNC operator keeps setups, problem solving and final checks; searching, media handling and offset cards shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using terminal calls and pick lists
role.ambitious_version: An operator who prepares the next job while the current one runs, with everything listed on screen.
